plan.contextChunk: This figure is a coordinate plane carrying four straight lines, each in a different color with arrowheads on both ends and tagged with a Roman numeral. The horizontal axis is labeled x and numbered from -7 to 7, the vertical axis is labeled y and numbered from -5 to 5, and a light gray unit grid fills the plotting region. Line I is orange and by far the steepest, rising from below the x-axis at the lower left and exiting through the top of the grid just right of the y-axis, where its label sits. Line II is light blue and the shallowest, entering at the left near x equal to -6.5 on the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at 3, and climbing to about x equal to 4, y equal to 5. Line III is teal, crossing the y-axis at -3 and the x-axis near x equal to 1.5 before rising to that same upper right region. Line IV is dark blue and the only line with a negative slope, entering at the upper left, crossing the y-axis at 3, and descending to roughly x equal to 4, y equal to -4.5. Color and numeral identify the lines, leaving steepness and direction as the properties to read off. The plot supports an exercise in pairing four given linear equations with the correct lines.

interactionPlan.concept: A linear equation y = mx + b is fully determined by its slope m (direction and steepness) and y-intercept b (where it crosses the y-axis), and matching an equation to one of four graphed lines means reading off exactly those two numbers.
elements: x-axis labeled 'x', numbered -7 to 7, with arrowhead
y-axis labeled 'y', numbered -5 to 5, with arrowhead
light gray unit grid over the plotting region
Line I: orange, very steep positive slope (~3), y-intercept ~2, arrowheads both ends, Roman numeral 'I' near its top
Line II: light blue, shallow positive slope (~0.5), y-intercept 3, Roman numeral 'II' near its top right
Line III: teal, moderately steep positive slope (~2), y-intercept -3, Roman numeral 'III' near its top right
Line IV: dark blue, negative slope (~-2), y-intercept 3, Roman numeral 'IV' near its lower right
candidate line (dashed purple) controlled by the slope and intercept sliders, pivoting about its y-intercept
rise-over-run marker (right triangle with 'rise' and 'run' labels) shown on the clicked line
y-intercept highlight dot on the clicked or candidate line

interactions.label: Slope m
interactions.teaches: Slope controls direction and steepness: positive m rises left to right, negative m falls, and larger |m| means a steeper line — rotating the candidate line shows which Roman-numeral line a given m could match

interactions.label: y-intercept b
interactions.teaches: The y-intercept slides the whole line up or down without changing its tilt, and it is what distinguishes lines with the same direction — e.g. lines II and IV both cross at y = 3 while line III crosses at y = -3
Clicking a labeled line reveals its rise-over-run triangle and y-intercept, connecting its visual steepness and crossing point to concrete values of m and b that an equation must have to match it

demo_steps.title: Read the four lines
demo_steps.narration: Four lines share the plane: I, II, and III rise left to right (positive slope) while IV falls (negative slope). Line II is the shallowest, line I the steepest.

demo_steps.title: Inspect a line
demo_steps.narration: Click line II: a rise-over-run triangle appears showing about 1 unit up for every 2 units right, and its y-intercept dot sits at 3 — so its equation must look like y = 0.5x + 3.

demo_steps.title: Match slope by rotating
demo_steps.narration: Drag the slope slider and watch the candidate line pivot about its intercept: negative values tilt it down like line IV, and steepening it brings it toward lines III and then I.

demo_steps.title: Match intercept by sliding
demo_steps.narration: Lines II and IV both cross the y-axis at 3, but line III crosses at -3. Slide b down to -3: the candidate shifts parallel to itself, showing b moves a line without changing its slope.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Two numbers completely pin down a line: b tells you where it crosses the y-axis and m tells you its direction and steepness — so matching an equation to a graphed line is just reading those two features off the picture.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Standard coordinate plane with unit gridlines, x from -7 to 7, y from -5 to 5, axis labels italic 'x' and 'y' at the positive ends. Four double-arrowed lines in distinct colors: orange line I steepest positive (roughly slope 3, intercept ~2, exiting top near x=1), light blue line II shallowest (slope ~0.5, intercept 3), teal line III steep positive (slope ~2, intercept -3), dark blue line IV the only negative slope (~-2, intercept 3). Roman numerals sit just past each line's upper (or for IV, lower-right) endpoint in matching color. The slider-driven candidate line should render as a dashed purple line with a visible pivot dot at its y-intercept so rotation about b is obvious. Rise-over-run markers appear as a small right triangle along the clicked line with 'rise' and 'run' labels; only one line's marker shows at a time.

authoredContext:
Match each equation of the linear functions with one of the lines in the figure.

A coordinate plane with x and y axes ranging from -7 to 7 and -5 to 5 respectively. Four lines, labeled I (orange), II (light blue), III (teal), and IV (dark blue), are shown. Line I and Line IV intersect at (0, 3). Line III and Line IV intersect at (1.5, 0). Line II and Line III intersect at (4, 5).
